subject: business-studies
title: Discounted Cash Flow and NPV
welcome_lead: Money today is worth more than money tomorrow - discount it.
meta_desc: A-Level Investment Appraisal: NPV and discounting.
final_note: NPV adjusts for time and risk - accept projects where NPV is positive.

concepts.def: Cash today is worth more than the same cash later.
Rate used to convert future cash to present value.
1 / (1 + r)^n - used to discount year-n cash flow.
Future cash flow discounted to today's value.
Sum of discounted cash flows minus initial outlay.
Accept if NPV greater than zero; pick highest NPV.

walkthroughs.body_html: Future cash is uncertain and could earn interest if held today. The discount rate reflects the cost of capital and risk - typically 8 to 12 percent for ordinary businesses.
Apply the discount factor to each year's cash flow, sum the present values, then subtract the initial outlay. A positive NPV adds shareholder value.
NPV uses cash, not profit, and reflects timing. But it depends heavily on the chosen discount rate and forecast cash flows - both prone to optimism bias.

mcqs.q: A positive NPV means a project:
options: Should be rejected
Adds shareholder value at the chosen discount rate
Has zero risk
Has the shortest payback

mcqs.q: The discount factor for year n at rate r is:
options: (1 + r) x n
r x n

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.

mcqs.q: What is Taylor's theory of scientific management?
options: Taylor said workers are motivated by recognition and teamwork.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Workers are motivated primarily by money; efficiency is maximised by breaking tasks into standardised steps, training workers in 'the one best way', and using piece-rate pay.
